summary.headline: FY26 total income rose 37.19% to INR256.92 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed to about 11% in H2 on forex and RCN prices; management guides 15-16%.
summary.overview: Pajson Agro's first earnings call after its December listing covered FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026). Total income grew 37.19% YoY to INR256.92 crore, EBITDA grew 24.98% and PAT grew 21.4%, with the company maintaining a double-digit full-year EBITDA margin. H2 saw margin compression from a spike in raw cashew nut (RCN) prices, forex movement (rupee moved about 10.5% from April 2025 base) and shipping disruptions, with H2 total income up 37.38% to INR138.5 crore and H2 PAT up 8.97%. Capacity utilisation was 86% on an 18,000 MT Andhra Pradesh plant, and a greenfield 35,000 MT Vizianagaram facility (targeting 70,000 MT total by FY30) is being built with INR39.53 crore of POs committed by March 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Double-digit full-year EBITDA margin (exact value not stated)

financial_highlights.metric: Average realisation per kg RCN processed

segments.name: Institutional B2B (cashew kernels)
segments.commentary: Serves large confectionery and snack manufacturers as the high-volume base; about 78% of repeat revenue comes from existing customers, per management. Customer visibility is only 1 to 3 months, and new capacity has no committed orders yet.

segments.name: Distribution / Royal Mewa brand (dry fruits)
segments.commentary: Brand revenue grew about 6.5x in FY26; distribution network covers over 170 distributors across 20+ states. Online presence on Amazon and Jio; quick-commerce listings (Blinkit, Zepto) in process.

guidance_outlook: Steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 15% to 16% for FY27, with management saying it expects a couple of percentage points of improvement in FY28 from scale; no exact number given.
Existing 18,000 MT capacity expected to grow revenue about 20% in FY27 (about 20% to 22% from current levels per different answers).
New Vizianagaram plant: trial production November or December 2026 (FY27), commercial production from Q4 FY27; utilisation about 15% in FY27, 65-70% in FY28, 85-90% the year after.
Peak revenue potential from new capacity about INR475 crore at 85% utilisation; management also said revenue at 70% utilisation for FY28 would be lower.
Debt-to-equity currently about 0.25, which management wants to stay within; working capital to be funded mainly by internal accruals, supplier credit and some borrowing growth.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity: 8,500 MT (FY23), 12,000 MT (FY24 and FY25), 18,000 MT (FY26). FY26 utilisation 86%.

Total capex for the new capacity about INR76 crore excluding land (land acquired in FY25). IPO proceeds of about INR74.45 crore: INR57 crore for the new facility, INR10.42 crore for general corporate purposes.
POs issued to vendors as of 31 March 2026 about INR39.5 crore, with advances of about INR10.5 crore paid; further POs of INR20-25 crore planned in Q1 FY27.
Machinery sourcing: some from Vietnam, some from China, about 40-45% indigenous from India. Greenfield line capacity of 100 tons per line, with automation targeted.
Plan to reach 70,000 MT capacity by FY30 with a near-zero-waste ecosystem.
demand_pricing: Average RCN realisation about INR161.5/kg in FY26 vs about INR160/kg in FY25; kernel realisation about INR660/kg; average kernel yield 24.57%.

Raw material sourcing: about 93-94% imported from West Africa (Cote d'Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau and others) and 6-8% domestic Indian crop in the last year; about 60% sourced from Cote d'Ivoire and Guinea-Bissau per Chairman.
Management said India consumes 2.0-2.2 million tons of RCN vs 400-500 thousand tons domestic production, so Indian prices track West African prices.

Margin pressure came from forex (rupee moved about 10.5%), RCN price spikes in H2, IPO expenses charged to P&L and shipping costs; management says part of the cost is being passed to customers via price increases and part to suppliers.
No exports in FY26 (some cargoes in FY25); export plans tied to new plant.

qa_highlights.question: How much of new capacity is backed by customer orders?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm orders yet; institutional visibility is only 1-3 months. Repeat revenue is about 78% from existing customers, and management says it is unable to serve all new demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and inventory rise?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 plant was shut for expansion and stock was sold off. FY26 focused on institutional customers, which carry more credit. Inventory about INR38 crore and debtors about INR18 crore; creditors rose to about INR20 crore from INR3 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of West Asia crisis and forex on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shipments come directly from Africa to India, so no supply disruption. Forex (procurement side, since raw material is imported) drove the margin dip; hedging via banks is being initiated and shipping lines approached for longer-term contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 15-16% EBITDA for FY27 and a couple of percentage points improvement in FY28 from scale.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the new facility and deployment of IPO funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction on schedule and structure ordered; POs of about INR39.5 crore issued by March, advances of about INR10.5 crore, and INR20-25 crore more POs in Q1 FY27. Trial production targeted November or December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Short-term borrowing and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR20 crore short-term working capital from bankers; the rate was about 8.4% last year and management said it has come down about 25 bps this year. Short-term loans and advances of INR31.95 crore were advances to suppliers in February.

risks_watch: Forex: rupee depreciation raises import cost for RCN; hedging policies not yet fully in place.
Shipping and fuel costs linked to Middle East disruption, though management says West African routes are unaffected.
Customer visibility is only 1-3 months and new capacity has no committed orders; ramp-up to 85-90% utilisation depends on demand.
Rising trade receivables and inventory (working capital intensity) as institutional sales expand on credit.
Execution risk on the Vizianagaram plant: trial production Nov-Dec 2026, commercial Q4 FY27, and remaining capex and POs of about INR20-25 crore in Q1 FY27.
Royal Mewa brand growth may require higher advertising spend, which management says will be kept within the 15-16% margin band.
Management's answers on the new capacity's revenue and margin profile were not consistent across the call (for example, 20% vs 20-22% growth and the INR475 crore peak revenue figure).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, capacity and the brand, but cautious on margins, which were guided down to 15-16% and attributed mainly to forex and RCN price swings. Answers on new-plant revenue and margin differentiation were sometimes vague or inconsistent, and some numbers were corrected or restated during the Q&A.
key_quotes: We are operating in a perform or perish era and Pajson is firmly in the perform category.
So we expect the margins to be steady.
We have the capacity, we have the brand, and now we have the capital.

growth.why: Management guides about 20% revenue growth from the existing 18,000 MT plant in FY27 at 86% utilisation, plus a 35,000 MT Vizianagaram plant (INR76 crore capex, about INR39.5 crore POs placed) with commercial production from Q4 FY27, though new capacity has no committed orders yet and only INR39.5 crore of POs is placed so far.
